title: Tuna Melt
subtitle: Creamy tuna salad on toast under bubbling cheddar
excerpt: Tinned tuna mixed with mayonnaise and a little onion, piled on white toast and grilled until the cheddar bubbles and browns. A diner classic that takes ten minutes.
sourceNotes: American diner open sandwich, a staple of lunch menus across the United States since the 1960s.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The tuna mixture can be made up to a day ahead and kept covered in the fridge.

content.text: The tuna melt is a diner open sandwich of creamy tuna salad under grilled cheddar. It gives a hot, satisfying lunch in under 15 minutes. Drain the tuna well so the toast does not go soggy under the filling.
Heat the grill to its highest setting.
Drain the tuna well. Press it against the side of a sieve to remove as much liquid as possible.
Mix the tuna, mayonnaise, red onion, celery if using, mustard, lemon juice, salt and pepper in the small bowl. Stir until combined.
Place the toasted bread slices on the baking tray. Lay a slice of tomato on each piece if using.
Spoon the tuna mixture onto each slice, spreading it to the edges.
Top each slice generously with grated cheddar. Place under the grill for 3 to 4 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and golden in patches.
Serve immediately while the cheese is still hot and molten.

items.symptom: The toast goes soggy under the filling.
items.cause: The tuna was not drained thoroughly.
items.fix: Drain the tuna in a sieve and press out the liquid firmly before mixing. A wet tuna mixture ruins the toast.

items.symptom: The cheese did not melt before the edges of the bread burned.
items.cause: The tray was too far from the grill element.
items.fix: Move the rack to the highest position so the cheese is close to the heat. Watch constantly after 2 minutes.

items.cause: Not enough seasoning or the lemon juice was omitted.
items.fix: Add the mustard and lemon juice. Both lift the flavour. Taste the mixture before it goes on the toast.
